_comment: Research v3 (cross-family): cooling-power curve points, data for representable_only models, catalog corrections, and method proposals. Written by a research subagent on 2026-11-01. Proposals are stored in not_found with key 'proposal:<name>' (schema workaround). New vocabulary keys/shapes used here are flagged in each record's reasoning and must be added to data/capability_vocabulary.json before import: cooling_power.at_120mK, cooling_power.at_500mK, cooling_power.at_1000mK (shape max, unit nW, at_temperature), magnetic_field.envelope (new 'envelope' shape), pressure.base.vs_temperature (new 'points' shape).

records.claim: Bluefors LD250 cooling power at 120 mK is 360 uW (third point of the documented cooling-power curve: 10 uW at 20 mK, 250 uW at 100 mK, 360 uW at 120 mK).
records.document_title: User Manual LD System, January 12, 2022, Version 2.0 (Bluefors Oy, BF1000-1234517327-9)
records.location: PDF page 6 (printed 'USER MANUAL | LD SYSTEM | 2 (48)'), Section 2.1 General description, Table 1: Main technical characteristics, LD250 column, row 'Cooling power at 120 mK'
records.quote: Table 1: Main technical characteristics Base temperature: Cooling power at 20 mK: Cooling power at 100 mK: Cooling power at 120 mK: LD250 10 mK 10 µW 250 µW 360 µW LD400 10 mK 12 µW 400 µW 575 µW
records.reasoning: Same table and document as the catalog's ev_bf_0004/ev_bf_0005, so it applies to exactly this configuration. Corroborated by the archived bluefors.com LD page (https://web.archive.org/web/2024id_/https://bluefors.com/products/dilution-refrigerator-measurement-systems/ld-dilution-refrigerator-measurement-system/), table 'LD250 | Guaranteed | Expected', row 'Cooling power at 120 mK | 360 μW | 400 μW'; the guaranteed figure is used. The PDF text layer renders the micro sign as an undecodable glyph; the quote restores µ. NEW VOCABULARY KEY REQUIRED: cooling_power.at_120mK {shape max, unit nW, better higher, at_temperature {120, mK}}. resolve_slots() already uses only installed cooling_power keys with an at_temperature, so with this key a Joule-heating or wiring check at 120 mK <= T_op < 4.2 K uses 360 uW instead of the 100 mK figure (250 uW).
records.found_via: tavily_search + tavily_extract (web.archive.org 2024 snapshot of bluefors.com) ; manual PDF fetched with curl and read with pdftotext (pages 5-7)

records.claim: The Dilution Refrigerator insert (DynaCool D850 / PPMS P850) provides 0.25 uW at the sample stage at 100 mK; it is an orderable option that none of these catalog configurations includes.
records.value_as_printed: 0.25 μW at sample stage at 100 mK
records.document_title: PPMS Family Measurement Options (Quantum Design, 1084-500 Rev. J0)
records.location: PDF page 22, 'Sub-Kelvin Capabilities - Dilution Refrigerator DynaCool (D850) / PPMS (P850)', Dilution Refrigerator Specifications, Operational Capabilities, row 'Cooling Power'
records.quote: Cooling Power: 0.25 μW at sample stage at 100 mK ... Operational Range: 0.05 to 4 K; 0 to 14 T ... Also compatible with PPMS® (P850) legacy systems.
records.reasoning: Option figure (insert sample stage), so install = optional_not_installed for every DynaCool and classic PPMS configuration (none lists a DR insert). resolve_slots() ignores non-installed cooling_power keys, so this cannot become the Joule-heating slot of the base system; it lets Lean explain that a 100 mK experiment needs the DR option (not_installed_never_passes) and lets Z3 propose a modified configuration. Single-point figure; no curve published.
records.found_via: tavily_search + tavily_extract (qdusa.com and qd-uki.co.uk copies) ; qdusa PDF fetched with curl and read with pdftotext (pages 21-22)

records.claim: CRX-VF documented field-versus-temperature envelope: +/-2.5 T at 10 K; +/-2 T from 11 K to 400 K; +/-1 T from 401 K to 420 K.
records.value_as_printed: ±2.5 T | 10 K | Up to 6 probe arms installed; ±2 T | 11 K to 400 K; ±1 T | 401 K to 420 K
records.document_title: CRX-VF probe station specifications (Lake Shore Cryotronics)
records.location: Specifications page, 'Temperature' table with columns Magnetic field | Temperature range | Configuration (footnote 1: base temperature assumes heat load for probes thermally anchored as listed in the probing section)
records.quote: Magnetic field Temperature range Configuration ±2.5 T 10 K Up to 6 probe arms installed ±2 T 11 K to 400 K ±1 T 401 K to 420 K
records.reasoning: First documented field-temperature envelope table in the catalog (the text is already in ev_ls_0004, but no table was imported, so field_temperature_envelope is representable_only). Implementation: slot = the segment whose [lo, hi] contains operating_temperature; relation B_required <= segment max; validity lo <= T_op and T_op <= hi re-checked by Lean exactly like the cooling-power slot validity, so a wrong segment can only give UNSUPPORTED. Gaps 10 K < T < 11 K and 400 K < T < 401 K are undocumented and must stay UNKNOWN. NEW VALUE SHAPE REQUIRED ('envelope': ordered closed temperature intervals with a field maximum) and new key magnetic_field.envelope. See also the correction on lakeshore_crx_vf magnetic_field.max.
records.found_via: tavily_extract (advanced) of the Lake Shore specification page

records.claim: CRX-VF vacuum with the standard TPS-FRG pump: below 5e-4 Torr at room temperature, below 1e-5 Torr at base temperature and below 1e-5 Torr at maximum temperature.
records.value_as_printed: Room temperature <5 × 10-4 Torr; Base temperature <1 × 10-5 Torr; Maximum temperature <1 × 10-5 Torr (Standard TPS-FRG)
records.document_title: CRX-VF probe station specifications (Lake Shore Cryotronics)
records.location: Specifications page, vacuum table, 'Standard TPS-FRG' column, rows Room temperature / Base temperature / Maximum temperature
records.quote: Standard TPS-FRG PS-HV-CPX option ... Room temperature <5 × 10-4 Torr <5 × 10-6 Torr Base temperature <1 × 10-5 Torr <5 × 10-7 Torr Maximum temperature <1 × 10-5 Torr <5 × 10-7 Torr
records.reasoning: Supplies p_base by cryostat state/temperature, the data the vacuum_at_temperature model lacks. Bounds are upper bounds; converted to uPa with CEILING rounding (1e-5 Torr = 1333.2237 uPa -> 1334; 5e-4 Torr = 66661.184 uPa -> 66662), which is conservative for a lower-is-better bound; exact Torr values are given in 'exact' (units.py defines Torr exactly as 101325/760 Pa). 'Room temperature' is the warm station (no cryopumping); base and maximum temperature are with the CCR running, so the model should key on cryostat state as well as sample temperature; intermediate sample temperatures between 10 K and 420 K are not individually documented, so a strict model may only use the two endpoints. The PS-HV-CPX high-vacuum option values are not recorded because this configuration uses the standard pump. NEW KEY/SHAPE REQUIRED: pressure.base.vs_temperature ('points').
records.found_via: tavily_extract (advanced) of the Lake Shore specification page

records.document_title: T96 System Controller Manual, Linkam Scientific Instruments User Guide 1.1.0 (© 2017 Linkam Scientific Ltd.; copy hosted by the Czech Technical University in Prague, FEL)
records.location: Printed page 13, section 'LNP96 Liquid Nitrogen Pump' > 'System overview' parts list, item 2
records.quote: System overview Please check that all of the following parts have been supplied with the LNP96 System. 1. LNP96 Liquid Nitrogen Pump 2. 2L Dewar (7L or 25L Dewars are available)
records.reasoning: Supplies the dewar_volume term of the cryogen_consumption model (consumption_rate x duration <= dewar_volume) for both LNP96 configurations. The consumption rate itself is still undocumented (eg_071, pm_020), so the model stays UNSUPPORTED until a rate is found. The 2 L dewar is the supplied default; a 7 L or 25 L dewar would be a documented modification. Manufacturer manual hosted by a university, as the catalog already does for other manuals.
records.found_via: tavily_search (Linkam LNP96 consumption) + tavily_extract of the PDF

PPMS Hardware Manual 1070-150 Rev. QD 1084-500 Rev. J0, 1307-010 DynaCool brochure, DynaCool user manual 1307-110 (UCSB/KTH/WMU mirrors), qdusa app notes: base-system sample-chamber cooling power is never stated; only option inserts (He-3, DR) have cooling-power figures (recorded as optional_not_installed).

Lake Shore CRX spec pages ('2-stage closed cycle refrigerator (CCR) with 1 W cooling power at 4.2 K') and CCS datasheet (bare-head single points: 204 7 W at 20 K, 204N 3 W at 10 K, 408 1 W at 4.2 K, 415 1.5 W, 418 2 W): no multi-temperature curve for the installed 408 head; SHI RDK-408D2 capacity maps exist only as graphs on third-party hosts, so no values recorded.
Linkam T96 manual (CTU host), linkam.co.uk/lnp96 and LNP support pages, Linkam 2024-2025 product guide (scienceservices.de): no liquid-nitrogen consumption rate.

Vendor documents and NIST Cryogenic Material Properties pages: NIST gives Young's modulus fits (see proposal:nist_polynomial_fits_for_thermal_stress) but no allowable/yield stress; thermal_stress model still lacks sigma_allowed.

Lune search_papers, Consensus, alphaXiv discover_papers, Tavily: no peer-reviewed measured cooling-power curve for an LD250/LD400/LD450; Krinner et al. (EPJ Quantum Technol. 2019, arXiv:1806.07862) measured an XLD400 (13 uW at 20 mK, 540 uW at 100 mK at 1.0 mmol/s), a different model, so not recorded.

Junker, U. (2004) 'QUICKXPLAIN: Preferred Explanations and Relaxations for Over-Constrained Problems', AAAI-04, pp. 167-172, https://aaai.org/Papers/AAAI/2004/AAAI04-027.pdf ; correctness proof: Rodler, P. (2022) 'A formal proof and simple explanation of the QuickXplain algorithm', Artificial Intelligence Review, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9622537 . PROPOSAL: today's 'why it fails' card comes from Z3's unsat core, which is not guaranteed minimal and is computed over Z3's encoding rather than Lean's semantics. Run QuickXplain over the experiment's mandatory requirements and coupled relations with the compiled Lean checker as the consistency oracle (isConsistent(S) := the Lean verdict on the profile restricted to S is not REJECT), ordering constraints by CryoLean's trust model (user-entered and adjustable parameters first, manufacturer specifications last) so the returned conflict is the preferred minimal one. The predicate 'Lean reports a violation' is monotone in the constraint set (conjunctive semantics), which is QuickXplain's precondition. Add a Lean check 'minimal_conflict' (the set yields REJECT and every one-element removal does not) and, following Rodler's proof, port QuickXplain itself to Lean so the explanation procedure is verified, not only its output.

Liffiton, M.H., Sakallah, K.A. (2008) 'Algorithms for Computing Minimal Unsatisfiable Subsets of Constraints', Journal of Automated Reasoning 40:1-33, https://doi.org/10.1007/s10817-007-9084-z ; Liffiton, Previti, Malik, Marques-Silva (2016) 'Fast, flexible MUS enumeration' (MARCO), Constraints 21:223-250, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10601-015-9183-0 . PROPOSAL: report repairs as minimal correction sets (the minimal sets of requirements or parameters that must be relaxed) and reasons as MUSes, using the hitting-set duality (every MCS hits every MUS). In demo B (wiring heat budget) the MCSes include {n_flux_lines}, {n_drive_lines}, {design_margin}; each becomes a Z3 optimisation over only that subset and is re-verified by Lean (REQUIREMENTS_MET on the exact document), replacing the single heuristic suggestion. MARCO's partial enumeration returns the first few MCSes quickly at catalog scale (26 configurations x ~20 requirements), and the verdict card can state whether enumeration was complete.

Felfernig, A., Schubert, M., Zehentner, C. (2012) 'An efficient diagnosis algorithm for inconsistent constraint sets', AI EDAM 26(1):53-62, https://tugraz.elsevierpure.com/en/publications/n-efficient-diagnosis-algorithm-for-inconsistent-constraint-sets (preprint https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.09005); parallel variant Le et al. (2023) 'FASTDIAGP: An Algorithm for Parallelized Direct Diagnosis', AAAI-23. PROPOSAL: catalog search is a knowledge-based configuration task (C_KB = a configuration's documented capabilities and coupled models, C_R = the user's requirements). FastDiag computes a preferred minimal diagnosis (which user requirements to relax) directly, without enumerating conflicts first, using O(2d log2(n/d) + 2d) consistency checks; run it per configuration when ranking alternatives so near-misses read 'compatible if you relax {temperature >= 1.8 K}'. Consistency checks are Lean runs on reduced documents, optionally pre-filtered by Z3.

Gamba, E., Bogaerts, B., Guns, T. (2023) 'Efficiently Explaining CSPs with Unsatisfiable Subset Optimization', Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research, https://doi.org/10.1613/jair.1.14260 ; Bleukx, I. et al. (2026) 'Using Certifying Constraint Solvers for Generating Step-wise Explanations', AAAI-26, https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/38432 . PROPOSAL: choose explanations by cost, not only minimality: an optimal constrained unsatisfiable subset (OCUS) whose costs encode evidence trust (citing a manufacturer specification is cheap, a user-entered or inferred value expensive) and readability (single-capability checks before coupled relations). Render it step by step ('3 x (58*13 nW + 50*79 nW + 8*20 nW) = 14.592 uW'; '14.592 uW > 12 uW at 20 mK [ev_bf_0006]'; 'therefore REJECT'), each step an exact rational evaluation Lean already performs; as in Bleukx et al., derive the steps from a certifying proof log so each is independently checked, here by Lean.

JCGM 100:2008 'Evaluation of measurement data - Guide to the expression of uncertainty in measurement' (GUM), https://www.bipm.org/documents/20126/2071204/JCGM_100_2008_E.pdf ; Melquiond, G. (2008) 'Proving bounds on real-valued functions with computations', IJCAR 2008, LNAI 5195, https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-71070-7_2 . PROPOSAL: add an 'interval' value kind (lo, hi, basis in {guaranteed, typical, expected, measured with coverage factor}) and give Lean a three-valued interval semantics over exact rationals: PASS only if the requirement holds at the pessimistic end of every interval, FAIL only if it fails at the optimistic end, otherwise NEED_MORE_INFORMATION, with soundness theorems (interval PASS implies PASS for every point value; interval FAIL implies FAIL for every point). Cases found in this research: Krinner's per-line loads with uncertainties (MXC drive line 0.013(6) uW -> [0.007, 0.019] uW, currently central values only), Bluefors 'Guaranteed 575 uW / Expected 650 uW at 120 mK', OptistatDry cold head 0.16 W (50 Hz) / 0.2 W (60 Hz), DynaCool base 1.8 K (60 Hz) / 1.85 K (50 Hz). Interval arithmetic on rationals is exact and its monotonicity lemmas are easy to prove in Lean (as Melquiond did in Coq with floating-point bounds).

Scholz, F.W. 'Statistical Tolerancing', University of Washington Stat 498B course notes (2008), https://faculty.washington.edu/fscholz/DATAFILES498B2008/TolerancingStat498B.pdf - contrasts arithmetic (worst-case) stacking TOL_S = TOL_1 + ... + TOL_n with root-sum-square stacking. PROPOSAL: wherever a coupled model adds uncertain terms (wiring heat budget sums, cooldown + run time, working distance + spacers, contraction mismatch), the trusted Lean verdict should use worst-case stacking of interval bounds, which is sound with no distributional assumption; RSS stacking assumes independent, centred, normally distributed errors that vendors do not document, so it should appear only as an untrusted advisory margin (like Z3 output). Show both numbers on the verdict card so users see how much of a rejection comes from conservatism.

Benveniste, A. et al. (2018) 'Contracts for System Design', Foundations and Trends in Electronic Design Automation 12(2-3):124-400, https://doi.org/10.1561/1000000053 (summary https://www.nowpublishers.com/article/DownloadSummary/EDA-053). PROPOSAL: model each vendor figure as an assume-guarantee contract rather than a bare number: '>= 575 uW at 120 mK' under {measured at the experimental flange outside the mixing chamber, empty system, standard shields, default PT415}; '< 1e-5 Torr' under {CCR running, TPS-FRG pump}; '1.8 K base' under {60 Hz mains}. CryoLean's model 'validity' list already encodes one kind of assumption; generalise it so every capability carries assumption predicates over the configuration and experiment (mains frequency, installed wiring, cryostat state). Lean uses a guarantee only when its assumptions are discharged, otherwise NEED_MORE_INFORMATION; contract refinement gives a principled rule for combining a base instrument with an option insert (He-3, DR) whose contract replaces the base temperature and cooling guarantees.

OPC Foundation, OPC 30500-1 'OPC UA for Laboratory & Analytical Device Standard (LADS) - Part 1: Basics', https://reference.opcfoundation.org/specs/OPC-30500-1/4 ; Juchli, D. (2022) 'SiLA 2: The Next Generation Lab Automation Standard', in Smart Biolabs of the Future, Advances in Biochemical Engineering/Biotechnology 182, https://doi.org/10.1007/10_2022_204 . PROPOSAL: define a machine-readable cryostat capability profile aligned with these standards: each configuration becomes a LADS Device with FunctionalUnits (sample temperature control, magnet, vacuum, optical access) whose control-function ranges and engineering units carry CryoLean vocabulary keys, install state and evidence id/hash; expose the same as SiLA 2 Feature Definition (FDL) properties (e.g. MaximumField, CoolingPowerAt). Import: vendor- or facility-published LADS/SiLA descriptions enter CryoLean only as untrusted candidates that must pass the validation gate (quote + source document), reducing transcription work without weakening the trust model. Export: facilities publish their exact installed configuration (options, wiring, mains frequency) so verdicts bind to real instruments instead of catalog assumptions.

W3C (2013) 'PROV-O: The PROV Ontology', W3C Recommendation 30 April 2013, https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/ . PROPOSAL: record every transformation between the printed value and the Lean input as PROV activities (prov:wasDerivedFrom, prov:Activity): unit conversion, rounding, fit evaluation, choosing guaranteed over expected, reading an archived snapshot instead of the live page. This research found silent derivation issues that such records would expose: pressure bounds rounded down (1e-5 Torr = 1333.22 uPa stored as 1333 uPa; 1e-4 Torr = 13332.24 uPa stored as 13332 uPa), i.e. the catalog claims a slightly better vacuum than documented. With activities recorded, the validator can enforce 'rounding must be conservative in the key's better direction' and the verdict card can show the derivation chain.

NIST Cryogenic Material Properties, '6061-T6 Aluminum (UNS A96061)' https://trc.nist.gov/cryogenics/materials/6061%20Aluminum/6061_T6Aluminum_rev.htm and '304 Stainless (UNS S30400)' https://trc.nist.gov/cryogenics/materials/304Stainless/304Stainless_rev.htm . PROPOSAL: the thermal_stress model (E*|eps_s - eps_h| <= sigma_allowed) lacks elastic moduli. NIST gives Young's modulus as plain polynomials y = a + bT + cT^2 + dT^3 + eT^4 in GPa (6061-T6: a=7.771221E1, b=1.030646E-2, c=-2.924100E-4, d=8.993600E-7, e=-1.070900E-9, equation range 2-295 K, 1 % fit error; 304 SS: two branches, 5-57 K and 57-293 K). Unlike the log-polynomial conductivity fits, these are exactly representable in CryoLean's expression language (add/mul of operating_temperature with decimal literals), so Lean can evaluate E(T) exactly, with validity bounds equal to the fit's equation range and the 1 % fit error carried as an interval (proposal:interval_valued_specifications). Store coefficients in materials.json as reference_data; an allowable-stress table is still needed before validating the model.
